commands.shell_local: The desktop can keep the unsealed key in its long-lived process cache. A one-shot CLI process would discard that key immediately on exit, so its next mutation prompts normally instead.

commands.shell_local: The desktop can erase a key retained by its long-lived process. The CLI retains no key after any invocation exits, so it is already sealed at that boundary.
commands.equivalence: Process-lifetime credential-store control only; both shells retain no key after their process ends.

commands.shell_local: The desktop needs an IPC reply channel for its ambient prompt; the CLI passphrase source reads the controlling terminal directly, so there is no domain operation or subcommand to mirror.

commands.shell_local: The desktop confirmation spans IPC calls and must invalidate its pending capability explicitly; the CLI plans and confirms in one synchronous command and retains nothing when declined.
commands.equivalence: Confirmation-lifetime control only; both shells consume a plan only after confirmation.
